shlokas.translation: I would sooner give up my life, or you, Sītā, and Lakṣmaṇa with you, than break a promise once given, above all a promise given to the Brahmins.
shlokas.context: In the Daṇḍaka forest Sītā gently asks Rāma why he should take up arms against rākṣasas who have not harmed him. Rāma answers that he has promised the forest sages his protection, and a promise once given is not taken back.
shlokas.speaker: Rāma (to Sītā)

shlokas.translation: From that Aruṇa I was born, and Sampāti is my elder brother. Know me as Jaṭāyu, the son of Śyenī, O tamer of foes.
shlokas.context: At Pañcavaṭī a great vulture comes to Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa. He tells them his lineage down to Aruṇa, names his elder brother Sampāti, and offers to guard Sītā while the brothers are away.
shlokas.speaker: Jaṭāyu (to Rāma)

shlokas.translation: King, people who always say pleasant things are easy to find; but one who speaks what is unpleasant yet good for you, and one who will listen to it, are hard to find.
shlokas.context: Rāvaṇa asks Mārīca to help him carry off Sītā. Mārīca begins his warning: flatterers are many, but few will say the unwelcome truth, and fewer still will hear it. The same couplet returns in the Yuddha-kāṇḍa (vulgate 6.16.21), spoken by Vibhīṣaṇa to Rāvaṇa.
shlokas.speaker: Mārīca (to Rāvaṇa)
teaches: visarga dropped before a voiced sound

shlokas.translation: I call on Janasthāna, and on you, karṇikāra trees in flower: tell Rāma quickly that Rāvaṇa is carrying Sītā away.
shlokas.context: Carried off through the sky by Rāvaṇa, Sītā calls on the land of Janasthāna and its flowering karṇikāra trees to take her message to Rāma.
shlokas.speaker: Sītā (to the trees of Janasthāna)
teaches: present tense for what is happening now (harati)

shlokas.translation: Kadamba, have you perhaps seen my beloved, who loved the kadamba? If you know of her, tell me of fair-faced Sītā.
shlokas.context: Rāma finds the hut empty. Half mad with grief, he goes from tree to tree in the forest, asking each one whether it has seen Sītā.
shlokas.speaker: Rāma (to a kadamba tree)

shlokas.translation: Saumitri, good people who follow dharma, brave and ready to give refuge, are found everywhere, even among those born as animals.
shlokas.context: Jaṭāyu has died of the wounds he took fighting Rāvaṇa for Sītā. Over the body of the vulture king, Rāma tells Lakṣmaṇa that goodness and courage are found in every kind of creature.

shlokas.translation: Bull among men, tiger among men: for your sake I have gathered forest food of many kinds, grown on the banks of the Pampā.
shlokas.context: At her āśrama by the Pampā the aged ascetic Śabarī welcomes Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa. Her teachers had told her that Rāma would come; she tells him that she has gathered forest food for him.
shlokas.speaker: Śabarī (to Rāma)

shlokas.translation: If friendship pleases you, here is my arm held out. Let hand take hand, and let a firm bond be made between us.
shlokas.context: On Mount Ṛśyamūka, Hanumān brings Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa to Sugrīva. Sugrīva offers Rāma his friendship and holds out his arm; Hanumān then kindles a fire, and the two walk around it to seal the pact.
shlokas.speaker: Sugrīva (to Rāma)

shlokas.translation: Loosed by the mighty one, that gold-decked arrow pierced the seven sāla trees and the mountain slope, and went into the earth.
shlokas.context: Sugrīva doubts that anyone can defeat Vālī. To prove his strength, Rāma takes up his bow and looses a single arrow at a row of seven sāla trees. A moment later the arrow comes back to him.
shlokas.speaker: Narrator (Vālmīki)
teaches: past participle with an instrumental agent (visṛṣṭo balavatā)

shlokas.translation: From today, respect place and time; bear what is pleasant and what is not, endure joy and sorrow as they come, and live obedient to Sugrīva.
shlokas.context: Struck down by Rāma's arrow, the dying Vālī gives his son Aṅgada his last advice: to live wisely and patiently under his uncle Sugrīva, the new king.
shlokas.speaker: Vālī (to Aṅgada)

shlokas.translation: This earth, worn out by the summer heat and drenched with fresh rain, gives off vapour, like Sītā shedding tears as she burns with grief.
shlokas.context: The rains have come, and nothing can be done until they pass. Waiting on a hill near Kiṣkindhā, Rāma watches the steaming earth and thinks of Sītā.
shlokas.speaker: Rāma (to Lakṣmaṇa)
teaches: the double sense of bāṣpa (vapour / tears)

sources.name: vedapath.app Rāmāyaṇa reader (Devanagari vulgate text; appears to reproduce the IIT Kanpur valmiki.iitk.ac.in text)

sources.name: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, valmikiramayan.net (Gita Press-based vulgate; Devanagari page, words printed separately)
sources.note: Verse printed word-split under the misprinted marker ३-२८-७: एषा घर्म परिक्लिष्टा नव वारि परिप्लुता | सीता इव शोक संतप्ता मही बाष्पम् विमुंचति. Same words.

sources.name: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, critical-edition text, enjoylearningsanskrit.com (Devanagari + IAST)
sources.note: Critical edition 4.27.7: एषा धर्मपरिक्लिष्टा नववारिपरिप्लुता । सीतेव शोकसंतप्ता मही बाष्पं विमुञ्चति ॥ Same words except धर्म- for घर्म-, an e-text slip (the indology.info e-text line 04027007a reads dharmaparikliṣṭā too); "worn out by dharma" makes no sense beside "drenched by new rain".

provenance.notes: Two vulgate witnesses agree on every word (घर्म-, "summer heat"). Orthography: the IIT Kanpur text writes शोकसन्तप्ता and विमुञ्चति with class nasals (valmikiramayan.net: संतप्ता, विमुंचति). The critical-edition e-text's धर्मपरिक्लिष्टा is treated as an e-text error, not a reading.

shlokas.translation: By this token, best of monkeys, Janaka's daughter will see that you have come from me, and she will not be afraid.
shlokas.context: As the search parties set out, Rāma gives Hanumān his ring, engraved with his own name, as a token by which Sītā will know that Hanumān comes from him.
shlokas.speaker: Rāma (to Hanumān)

sources.name: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, valmikiramayan.net (Gita Press-based vulgate; Devanagari page, words printed separately)
sources.note: Verse ४-४४-१३ printed word-split: अनेन त्वाम् हरिश्रेष्ठ चिह्नेन जनकाअत्मजा | मत् सकाशात् अनुप्राप्तम् अनुद्विग्ना अनुपश्यति (जनकाअत्मजा is the page's display of जनक-आत्मजा). Confirms wording and number.

sources.name: Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, critical-edition text, enjoylearningsanskrit.com (Devanagari + IAST)
sources.note: Critical edition 4.43.12: अनेन त्वां हरिश्रेष्ठ चिह्नेन जनकात्मजा । मत्सकाशादनुप्राप्तमनुद्विग्नानुपश्यति ॥ Pāda text follows this letter for letter; the indology.info e-text (lines 04043012a/c) reads the same.

provenance.notes: Same words in both witnesses. The critical edition prints pādas 3–4 as one run (…प्राप्तमनुद्विग्ना…); by the game's convention the pāda break is stored at the word boundary (…प्राप्तम् | अनुद्विग्ना…). The research note reports the IIT Kanpur text with the same reading. The ring itself is described in the verse before (4.44.12: स्वनामाङ्कोपशोभितम् अङ्गुलीयम्).

shlokas.translation: From here, on an island in the ocean a full hundred yojanas away, stands the lovely city of Laṅkā, built by Viśvakarman.
shlokas.context: On the southern shore the searchers, ready to give up, meet Sampāti, Jaṭāyu's elder brother, whose eyes see far. He tells them where Sītā is held.
shlokas.speaker: Sampāti (to the vānaras)
teaches: locative of place and distance (dvīpe, śatayojane)
past participle with an instrumental agent (nirmitā viśvakarmaṇā)

shlokas.translation: Rise, tiger among monkeys, and leap across the great ocean, Hanumān; for your power of movement surpasses that of every living being.
shlokas.context: On Mount Mahendra the vānaras despair before the ocean that none of them can cross. Jāmbavān turns to Hanumān, reminds him of his birth and his power, and urges him to leap.
shlokas.speaker: Jāmbavān (to Hanumān)
teaches: imperative uttiṣṭha (as in the Bāla verse uttiṣṭha naraśārdūla)

provenance.notes: Same words in both witnesses (valmikiramayan.net spells लंघयस्व with anusvāra). The research note reports the IIT Kanpur text with the same reading. Pairs with s-kausalya-supraja (उत्तिष्ठ नरशार्दूल): the same "rise, tiger among …" formula.
